newsitem.title: LATVIA: CENTRAL BANK TO TIGHTEN DEPOSIT REGULATIONS.
newsitem.headline: CENTRAL BANK TO TIGHTEN DEPOSIT REGULATIONS.

text.p: Latvia's central bank said on Wednesday that it was considering taking steps to tighten regulations for banks licenced to take deposits from individuals.
"These days some of the criteria have become too mild," Ilmar Rimshevics, the deputy president of the central bank, told a news conference.
"We are considering making the mandatory basic capital level equal to that for setting up a new commercial bank - five million lats," he said.

Latvia's central bank, stung by criticism after tens of thousands of depositors lost their savings when the country's largest commercial bank collapsed in 1995, said it was determined to prevent any further shocks to the sector.
Rimshevics said that the country's banking sector had recovered from the crisis but tighter regulations were needed to ensure that similar problems did not arise in the future.
Currently 16 of Latvia's 31 banks are fully licenced and allowed to take deposits from individuals.
